exposure: Dietary intake (fruits, vegetables, junk food, dairy products)
outcome: Concentration of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium in stool
cohort: 79 children aged 6 to 36 months, divided into two groups: 39 children with chronic constipation (cases) and 40 children without constipation (controls)
finding: Children with chronic constipation had a lower concentration of Lactobacillus in their stools and consumed more dairy products compared to non-constipated children.
mod_finding: Constipated children were more frequently delivered via caesarean section (69.2%).
